title: What did Java 17 add overall, and why do teams adopt it (LTS stability + modern features)?

s1_definition.profdef: Java 17 is LTS (Long-Term Support). Key features finalized: (1) RECORDS (Java 16) — immutable data carriers replacing POJO boilerplate, (2) SEALED CLASSES (Java 17) — restrict which classes can extend/implement, (3) PATTERN MATCHING INSTANCEOF (Java 16) — `if (obj instanceof Trade t)` combines check+cast, (4) SWITCH EXPRESSIONS (Java 14) — return values, no fall-through, (5) TEXT BLOCKS (Java 15) — multi-line strings without escaping. Also: strong encapsulation of JDK internals, removal of deprecated APIs, and the new macOS/AArch64 port.
s1_definition.oneliner: Java 17 LTS: records, sealed classes, pattern matching instanceof, switch expressions, text blocks. LTS = enterprise-grade stability for years.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Java 17 is LTS (Long-Term Support). Key features finalized: (1) RECORDS (Java 16) — immutable data carriers replacing POJO boilerplate, (2) SEALED CLASSES (Java 17) — restrict which classes can extend/implement, (3) PATTERN MATCHING INSTANCEOF (Java 16) — `if (obj instanceof Trade t)` combines check+cast, (4) SWITCH EXPRESSIONS (Java 14) — return values, no fall-through, (5) TEXT BLOCKS (Java 15) — multi-line strings without escaping. Also: strong encapsulation of JDK internals, removal of deprecated APIs, and the new macOS/AArch64 port.

**One line to remember:** Java 17 LTS: records, sealed classes, pattern matching instanceof, switch expressions, text blocks. LTS = enterprise-grade stability for years.

sections.s2_technical:
Java 17 (LTS) consolidates several preview features into finals. Records (JEP 395) are immutable data carriers: `record Trade(String id, BigDecimal amount) {}` auto-generates the constructor, accessors, `equals`, `hashCode`, and `toString`. Sealed classes/interfaces (JEP 409) restrict which types may extend or implement them: `sealed interface Instruction permits Buy, Sell`, enabling exhaustive handling.

Pattern matching for `instanceof` (JEP 394) binds the cast in the test: `if (o instanceof Trade t) { use t; }` removes the explicit cast. Switch expressions (final earlier) and text blocks round out the ergonomics. Java 17 also finalised the strong encapsulation of JDK internals and made the new macOS/AArch64 ports available.

A banking example: modelling a settlement message as a `sealed interface` permitting `EquityTrade`, `FxTrade`, and `Derivative` records, then handling them with a pattern-matching `instanceof` or exhaustive `switch`, so adding a type without handling it is a compile error. Senior nuance: records + sealed + pattern matching together give algebraic-data-type style modelling with exhaustiveness checking — the enterprise-standard baseline since most shops moved from Java 8 to Java 17 LTS.
sections.s3_banking: Problem — Trade DTOs were verbose boilerplate classes, and a chain of `instanceof` casts over a trade hierarchy was error-prone and silently incomplete. Fix: Java 17 records remove the DTO boilerplate, sealed interfaces restrict the hierarchy, and pattern-matching `instanceof` binds the cast and supports exhaustive handling.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Input: a Buy(50000) and a Sell(20000) instruction, modelled as records under a sealed interface.

**Step 2.** Each record auto-generates its constructor, accessor, equals, hashCode, and toString — no boilerplate.

**Step 3.** The sealed `Instruction` permits only Buy and Sell, so the hierarchy is closed and checkable.

**Step 4.** `i instanceof Buy b` tests and binds `b` in one step, removing the explicit cast.

**Step 5.** The handler returns BUY 50000 and SELL 20000.

```text
INFO: BUY 50000 ; SELL 20000
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ JAVA 17 LTS — KEY FEATURES ═══

  Feature                       │ Java │ Replaces
  ──────────────────────────────│──────│──────────────────────
  Records                       │ 16   │ POJO boilerplate (getters, equals, hashCode)
  Sealed classes                │ 17   │ Unrestricted inheritance
  Pattern matching instanceof   │ 16   │ Explicit cast after instanceof
  Switch expressions            │ 14   │ Switch statement + break
  Text blocks                   │ 15   │ String concatenation + escaping

  WHY JAVA 17:
  ├─ LTS: 8+ years of security patches
  ├─ Spring Boot 3.x REQUIRES Java 17+
  ├─ Most libraries support 17 (battle-tested)
  └─ Next LTS = 21 (more aggressive — virtual threads)
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Java 17 is the LTS release that brings modern language features to enterprise Java. Records eliminate POJO boilerplate (automatic constructor, getters, equals, hashCode, toString). Sealed classes restrict inheritance to a known set of subtypes — enabling exhaustive switch. Pattern matching instanceof combines type check and cast in one expression. Switch expressions return values and eliminate fall-through. Text blocks handle multi-line strings cleanly. Teams adopt Java 17 because it's LTS (years of support), Spring Boot 3.x requires it, and it's the sweet spot between modern features and stability.
